title: Review: big overnight range -> NY takes the Asia high?
body: CONFIRMED as a fact, but no new information. It's real and stable (no look-ahead), but it runs the other way from the question: after a big overnight range NY takes the Asia high LESS often (64% vs 83%). The reason is mechanical: a big night usually leaves the Asia high farther from the open (and on a third of days the open is already above it, which counts as 'taken'). How far the Asia high is from the open predicts much better. With that distance held fixed, a busy night actually makes it slightly more likely - the usual 'busy night, busy day' effect. Stays in the morning read as context, not as an edge.
